curriculum.summary: What good design actually is, and the rules worth knowing before you break them.

lessons.title: Design principles that actually matter
lessons.description: Contrast, alignment, proximity and repetition, applied to real screens.

lessons.title: Color theory and typography for interfaces
lessons.description: Choosing palettes and type scales that stay readable on real devices.

lessons.title: Layout, grids and visual hierarchy
lessons.description: Using grids and spacing to tell the eye what to look at first.

takeaways: Read a layout like a designer
Pick type and colour with intent

curriculum.summary: How to design for real people instead of guessing what they want.

lessons.title: Understanding real users, not assumptions
lessons.description: Interview technique, and how to ask questions that get honest answers.

lessons.title: Personas and user journey maps
lessons.description: Turning research notes into personas and a journey you can design against.

lessons.title: Competitive and heuristic analysis
lessons.description: Auditing existing products to find the gaps worth designing for.

curriculum.summary: Get from a rough idea to a clickable prototype your mentor can review.

lessons.title: Low-fidelity wireframing
lessons.description: Sketching structure and flow before committing to any visual style.

lessons.title: Building interactive prototypes in Figma
lessons.description: Linking frames, states and transitions into something clickable.

lessons.title: Getting from idea to clickable flow fast
lessons.description: A repeatable process for going from brief to testable prototype.

takeaways: Build a clickable flow in Figma
Test an idea before you polish it

curriculum.summary: Turn wireframes into interfaces that look and behave like real products.

lessons.title: Design systems and component libraries
lessons.description: Building reusable components, variants and tokens in Figma.

lessons.title: High-fidelity UI design
lessons.description: Taking wireframes to polished screens with real content.

lessons.title: Accessibility basics every designer needs
lessons.description: Contrast ratios, touch targets and states that work for everyone.

curriculum.summary: Prove your design works, then package it into something you can show.

lessons.title: Running a usability test
lessons.description: Writing tasks, recruiting testers, and watching without leading them.

lessons.title: Iterating on real feedback
lessons.description: Turning test findings into specific, prioritised design changes.

lessons.title: Packaging your work into a portfolio piece
lessons.description: Writing up problem, process and outcome so a recruiter gets it.

projects.title: Mobile app onboarding flow
projects.description: Take a clunky sign-up and rebuild it around a real user journey, from first screen to activated account.

projects.title: End-to-end booking flow
projects.description: Search, selection and checkout as one connected journey — wireframed, then taken to high-fidelity UI.

projects.title: A mini design system
projects.description: Buttons, forms, cards and their states for a real product, documented and ready to hand to a developer.

faq.question: Who is this course for?
faq.answer: Anyone starting from scratch or leveling up — the curriculum starts with fundamentals and builds up to three portfolio projects.

faq.question: Do I need design experience to start?
faq.answer: No. The course assumes no prior design background and starts with the basics.

faq.question: Is the 100% refund real for this course too?
faq.answer: Yes — finish the five modules and submit your three projects inside 3 months, and Tutedude refunds 100% of your fee.

faq.question: What tools do I need?
faq.answer: Figma is used throughout the course. It's free to use for learning, and lessons walk you through it from the basics.
